title: perf(canary): automated detection of latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Jordan Blake
description:
Motivation: Reduce production regressions by automatically detecting latency and throughput degradations from continuous performance canaries and preventing unsafe rollouts. This PR implements an automated detector that evaluates canary time-series (p50/p95 latency, tokens/s throughput, error-rate) using threshold and statistical-drift heuristics, and wires those signals into rollout guards that can pause or rollback model/service rollouts when regressions are detected.

What changed: new canary detector + rules engine, integration with rollout service, improved instrumentation and dashboards, unit & integration tests, and docs. The description below summarizes the components and tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector: windowed comparison of baseline vs canary with configurable thresholds and Welch's t-test for latency regressions
- [x] Throughput detector: rate-based comparisons with hysteresis to avoid flapping
- [x] Rollout guard integration: pause/rollback API + reason codes 
- [x] Telemetry: new metrics (canary_detector{status,reason}, rollout_guard{action}), tracing hooks added
- [x] Tests: unit tests for detectors + end-to-end canary simulation test 
- [x] Docs: docs/perf/canary.md with config examples and operational runbook

Related: builds on ENG-1428 (canary pipeline refactor) and addresses SUP-9812 (customer-reported perf regression in dedicated).

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can we expose the detector window size as an override in the canary config? Some clients have bursty traffic. (requested change)
Jordan Blake: Added 'window_seconds' and documented rationale; default remains 300s to balance noise and detection speed.
Ethan Moore: The Welch's t-test approach seems reasonable but we should clip extreme outliers in latency samples before computing stats to avoid spurious signals. (requested change)
Jordan Blake: Added 99.9th percentile clipping and unit tests that simulate long-tail spikes.
Lena Garcia: Can the rollout guard provide an automated rollback path or just pause? We should be conservative for now.
Jordan Blake: Implemented pause + annotated suggestions for rollback; full auto-rollback is gated behind an enterprise flag and will be a follow-up (ENG-1582).
CI: All checks passed after fixes (build, unit tests, canary-sim integration).
release_notes: Add automated canary detectors and rollout guards to prevent latency/throughput regressions. Configurable thresholds, hysteresis to reduce flapping, and integration with rollout controller. Docs and dashboard included.
test_summary: Unit: 42 passed, 0 failed. Integration (canary-sim): 3 scenarios passed (no-regression, transient-spike, sustained-regression). CI: full pipeline green.
operational_impact: New metrics and dashboards; operators should review default thresholds in first 24h after deploy. Rollouts will now automatically pause on detected regressions; manual confirmation required for rollback unless enterprise flag enabled.
notes_for_release: Operators: monitor canary_detector{status} and rollout_guard{action} metrics; use docs/perf/canary.md to tune thresholds per workload.
risk_assessment: Medium: detector tuned conservatively with hysteresis to avoid false positives. Added canary-sim integration test to reduce regression risk. Auto-rollback disabled by default.
